- **Space Complexity:** $O(R \cdot (IJ + JK + KI))$ for storing the decomposed components and their convolved versions, significantly less than the $O(I \cdot J \cdot K)$ required for full volume reconstruction [S1][S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that naive 3D convolution requires a space complexity of $O(I, J, K)$ to store the full reconstructed volume. It further explains that the proposed method performs separable component-wise convolution, where the time complexity for computing convoluted components is $O(I, J, L_N + J, K, L_N + K, I, L_N)$. Since the decomposed tensor consists of $R$ components (vectors of size $I, J, K$ and matrices of size $I, J, J, K, I, K$), storing these components requires space proportional to $R(I + J + K + IJ + JK + KI)$. The claim's formula $O(R(IJ + JK + KI))$ correctly captures the dominant terms of the storage for the decomposed components (specifically the matrix components which are $O(RIJ)$, $O(RJK)$, $O(RKI)$). The evidence supports that this approach avoids the $O(IJK)$ storage of the full volume, thus the claim is supported.
